headline: High-risk data leakage and capability conflict: Copilot can read/write repo context while the paired content-writing agent has no documented isolation or runtime boundaries.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Profile A is a non-runnable content-writing repo with no I/O surfaces, while Profile B ingests editor buffers and repo context. A direct injection path is not documented, but if A’s content is manually copied into B or placed in shared files, B could misread it as instructions. The pairwise pathway is therefore limited and indirect.
conditions: IF content from agent_a is manually pasted into agent_b chat or editor buffers
IF a shared file is used as the bridge between agent_a output and agent_b input
mitigations: Keep agent_a outputs out of agent_b prompt context
Use a separate review note for agent_a content
Disable copy-paste of untrusted instructions into Copilot sessions
Mark imported text as data, not instructions

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent B reads repo context and open editor buffers and can write files; Agent A is a content-writing repository with no documented isolation or data-handling controls. If sensitive material is present in the shared workspace, B may ingest it into its inference context and transmit context to api.githubcopilot.com. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default editor workflows.
conditions: IF sensitive text is present in files or editor buffers accessible to agent_b
IF agent_b is used on the same workspace that contains agent_a-derived confidential material
mitigations: Remove secrets from the workspace before opening Copilot
Use a scrubbed copy of the repo for Copilot sessions
Restrict Copilot to non-sensitive projects
Review open buffers before enabling chat or workspace edits

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent B can write the filesystem and modify git state; Agent A has no runtime capabilities, so there is no symmetric conflict. However, if A’s generated artifacts are placed into the same repo or workspace, B’s edits can overwrite or race with them. Uncertainty remains because A’s operational surface is undocumented, so the safer medium rating is warranted.
conditions: IF agent_a artifacts are stored in the same git working tree that agent_b edits
IF multiple Copilot instances or humans modify the same files without locking
mitigations: Use separate branches for Copilot edits
Commit or stash A-generated files before Copilot runs
Avoid concurrent edits on the same files
Review git diffs before accepting Workspace changes

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent B’s Workspace plans and chat can turn context into edits, so if A’s content is fed into B as source material, B may act on it with limited verification. A is only a content-writing resource, but B’s edit/apply workflow creates a downstream action path. The interaction is inferred rather than directly evidenced, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF agent_a output is used as authoritative source text for agent_b
IF agent_b Workspace applies edits derived from agent_a without human review
mitigations: Require human review of all Copilot-applied edits
Cross-check A-derived claims against primary sources
Limit Copilot to refactoring tasks on verified code
Separate drafting from execution workflows

E_compliance.rationale: Agent B is a closed-source GitHub Copilot service with GitHub repo OAuth and vendor-only egress; Agent A is an open-source content-writing repo with no documented data residency or retention controls. No specific residency mismatch is proven, but the pair creates a compliance gap if regulated content is placed into Copilot context. A is not cited for a residency claim because none is documented.
conditions: IF regulated data is entered into agent_b editor buffers or chat
IF organizational policy forbids sending repo context to vendor-hosted AI services
mitigations: Do not use Copilot on regulated repositories
Check policy before enabling chat or Workspace
Strip personal or regulated data from open buffers
Use a local-only assistant for restricted projects
